headline: Customers can now download their own invoices as a spreadsheet file, and the change only shows each customer their own invoices.
what_changed: Signed-in customers can download a spreadsheet file (CSV) listing their invoices, for example to send to an accountant.
The file has four columns: invoice number, issue date, total in dollars-and-cents style (for example 199.00), and status (paid, open or void).
The file downloads under the name invoices.csv.
The existing invoice list on the customer's account page keeps the same information. Its code was tidied up so both views share one way of finding the invoices.
A small automated check was added for the new download. It only confirms the file type, not the file's contents.
questions_for_developer: Are all invoices in one currency? The spreadsheet's Total column shows numbers with no currency sign, so an accountant may need to know which currency it is.

Should void invoices appear in the download? The list already includes them, and the spreadsheet does too, with status 'void'. This matches the current list, so it is only a question of what customers expect.
good_news: The download only returns invoices that belong to the customer who is signed in. Each customer's invoices are kept separate from everyone else's.
Customers who are not signed in are turned away before any invoice data is read.
The change is small and contained. It adds one new download option and does not change what the existing list shows.
